newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans close weaker as funds sell late.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans close weaker as funds sell late.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures closed mostly lower on Wednesday, pressured by heavy fund selling late, traders said.
"The bean market was overbought and corrected," said Paul Haugens, vice president with FIMAT Futures.
Losses in new crop months were limited by gains in new crop corn. Traders noted November soybean and December corn futures prices over the next few weeks will help determine what farmers will plant.
Higher new crop corn favors increased corn acreage, so a rally in December corn prompted buying in November soybeans.
"The soybean complex will not stand still with corn going up," a trader said. "They'll follow it."
Active farmer selling sparked by Tuesday's 18-cent-per- bushel gains in soybeans contributed to losses and commercial selling was noted, floor sources said.
"The spreads are giving up," a trader said, referring to the March/May spread. "That tells us there's big country movement."
Soybeans ended eight cents per bushel lower to 1/2 cent higher with March off eight at $7.71 a bushel and new crop November down 1-1/2 at $7.03-1/4.
On the day, Cargill Inc sold 4.5 million bushels May and one million July. Cargill Investor Services sold five million bushels May.
Refco Inc was the largest seller on the day, accounting for eight million bushels May and four million March, traders said. Merrill Lynch sold five million bushels May.
In options trade, Goldenberg-Hehmeyer reportedly sold 700 May $8.00 calls at 15-1/4 to 15-1/2 cents.
Technical traders said short term signals remained bullish despite the lower close. The March contract closed well above the four- and 20-day moving averages.
They said resistance on Thursday would be at $7.80 per bushel in the March with support at $7.66.
Volume was estimated by CBOT at 78,000 contracts, compared with Tuesday's volume of 79,636 contracts.
